universe: every EDGAR entity that has filed at least one periodic report (10-K, 10-Q, 20-F, 40-F and their small-business and transition variants)

rules.merged_into: Entities A and B share a business-combination accession (425, DEFM14A, PREM14A, DEFM14C, PREM14C, DEFA14M, SC TO-T, SC TO-T/A, SC 14D9, SC 14D9/A, SC14D1F, SC 14D1). A files Form 15 or Form 25 within 730 days after their last shared filing, files no periodic report more than 120 days after that termination, and B files a periodic report after it. Direction is left unassigned when both or neither entity passes. When A passes against several counterparties, the one with the latest shared filing is the survivor; a tie leaves A unassigned.
rules.spun_off_from: A Form 10-12B/10-12G accession lists a second entity that files periodic reports; that entity is the parent.
rules.ceased_reporting: No periodic report in the 548 days before the as-of date, after at least one. Reason = latest terminal event (merged_into, bankruptcy_filed, deregistered, delisted), else undisclosed.

coverage_limits: EDGAR electronic filing began in 1993 and became mandatory for all domestic filers in May 1996; earlier history is absent.
8-K item numbers start in August 2004, so bankruptcy_filed misses earlier filings and any bankruptcy not reported on an 8-K.

merged_into needs a shared EDGAR accession. Acquisitions of private companies, and deals filed without one (for example a cash merger where only the target files a proxy), leave the target's exit undisclosed.
SIC codes are SEC's current assignment for each entity, not the code it held in each historical year.
